//: Canadian broadcast rights for Game Day North: which service carries each game.
This file is the only copy. build.js inlines it into the page, so every build of the
website and the iOS app carries it, and scripts/fetch-data.mjs copies it into data.json,
so a fix reaches installed apps on the next data refresh with no App Store review.
Rules: ordered, first match wins. A rule applies to games of its `comp` when every
condition in its `if` holds (no `if` = every game of that competition):
teams          any of these team ids is playing
day            the Eastern listing date (YYYY-MM-DD) is one of these
dow            the home team's local day of the week (0 = Sunday) is one of these
hourFrom       the local start hour is at least this
stage          true: the game carries a stage (a postseason round)
tournamentIs   the tournament's name is one of these (case-insensitive, whole name)
tournamentHas  the tournament's name contains one of these (case-insensitive)
major          true: a Grand Slam
An app that meets a condition it does not know skips that rule rather than guessing,
so adding a new kind of condition never makes an older app match too much.
carriers: [{name, kind: tv|stream, confidence?}]. confidence: confirmed | expected | unknown.
src: a key of `sources`. checked: the date a row was verified; a row without one
inherits the top-level `checked`. Set a per-row `checked` on the rows you verify;
do not move the top-level date, which would claim every other row was re-checked too.
services: the subscriptions a viewer buys. carrierService maps each carrier name to one.
Never rename a service id: viewers' saved choices are stored by id.
Keys named "//" are comments. The build strips them before anything ships.

//: — tennis —
Slam first: its rights are its own, whichever tour the draw sits in.
Tennis rights attach to a tournament, never to a player. Following
Alcaraz tells you nothing about who shows his matches; the tournament
he is playing decides that, and it changes from week to week. So these
rules key on the event, and a player's row inherits whatever the
tournament he is in resolves to.
Two sources were checked and neither covers everything, which is why
most of this table is honest about not knowing:
· ATP's own broadcaster list names TSN in Canada for the tour, and
Sportsnet for the Canadian Masters event specifically.
· The US Open's own international broadcaster page names TSN and RDS.
A Grand Slam is not an ATP tour event and its rights are sold
separately, so the ATP listing says nothing about Melbourne, Paris or
Wimbledon — those resolve to Coverage not confirmed rather than being assumed to
follow the tour. Neither source covers the WTA tour at all, so a WTA
event outside a Slam is unknown too. Guessing here would put a service
badge on a match nobody can confirm is carried.

//: — men's national teams —
A friendly is sold match by match, usually by the home federation,
so there is no competition-wide deal to read a carrier from. What
can be known is what a broadcaster has published, and TSN has
published Canada's fall lineup match by match, with channels.
So the rule keys on Canada being in the match, and then on what TSN
actually listed. The three matches it names are confirmed, on the
channels it names. A Canada match it does not name is expected on
TSN and no more than that: the article is a lineup, not a rights
announcement, and says nothing about a match after 6 October. Every
other nation's friendly is unknown, because nothing primary names a
Canadian carrier for it.
These rows carry their own date: they were sourced on 2026-09-29,
later than the rest of the table, and do not borrow the top-level date.
